idiom_name: structural role interfaces + per-core role registry (WeakMap); Proxy for transparent member lookup
implementation_notes: TypeScript's structural typing means a role needs no inheritance link to the core: a role view is simply an object satisfying an interface, composed per core in a WeakMap registry, and role combinations are expressed as intersections (`Customer & Borrower`) instead of an ever-growing Component interface. Mixins via class expressions or factory functions add a role's members at runtime, and a Proxy handler can forward unknown members to the registry so clients never see the lookup. The explicit classic structure remains justified when one uniform role protocol must be enforced across modules, when roles are persisted, or when runtime validation of role sets matters; intersections are erased at runtime, so a brand or explicit guard is needed if accidental structural matches are a risk.
pitfalls: The `as R` cast is unchecked and the registry stores `object`, so a wrong RoleId/type pairing compiles; validate or derive the type from the id.
Structural typing accepts any role-shaped object; without a brand or type guard, an unrelated object silently satisfies a role interface.
WeakMap keys by identity: a cloned or re-wrapped core gets an empty role set, and Proxy handlers must respect the get/set invariants or throw a TypeError.
